Drummer Earl Watkins was born in San Francisco on January 29, 1920. Since the mid-1940s he has been a major figure in the Bay area jazz scene and is well known for his association with Earl Hines and Kid Ory. Earl played an instrumental role in the 1960 merger of the white and black musicians’ union in San Francisco and continues to maintain an important role in the city as a musician and union executive.
Earl was interviewed in San Francisco, California on August 7, 2002 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
